Two topics, 25 minutes: the rule and the test, then four invented situations. Say it in one breath; the clock starts at the next slide. # The rule that isn't optional [10 min]{.time} {#the-rule}

::: notes
**Goal.** Everyone can say the privacy line, say what the law does and does not tell them in three sentences, and de-identify a sentence and re-read it as a stranger.

**Have ready.** A visible timer. The privacy checklist link is on the last slide, for afterwards; nothing in these ten minutes needs it.

**Clock.** 0:00 the line. 0:30 where it goes. 1:45 the law. 2:30 the list. 3:45 what it misses. 5:00 four steps. 5:30 mark the note. 7:30 the after. 8:00 beyond the text. 9:00 settings. 9:30 time.

**Watch for.** "There is no name, so it is fine": the list is a floor; the test is whether anyone could be identified. A legal debate: park it; the answer is always the data protection officer or legal team. Someone confessing a past paste: thank them, point to "If it already happened" on the checklist, and take the detail aside after the session.

**If asked.** An approved tool? One your institution vetted and contracted for patient information; ask which, and for what. A paid plan, or history off? No: a paid personal account is still a consumer tool, and settings do not change who approved it. Have I broken the law, and what are the penalties? Both are for your data protection officer or legal team; this course quotes no amounts or articles. If it already happened, the checklist steps apply.

**Bridge.** "That is the rule and the test. Now the situations where careful, well-meaning doctors break it without noticing: four short situations."
:::

## The privacy line {#privacy-rule .dark background-color="#0f172a"}

[No patient identifiers into a consumer AI tool. Ever. Full stop.]{.huge}

::: notes
**0:30.** Read the line aloud, slowly, then stop for three seconds. It is the one rule in this module that does not bend, and everything after it is how to keep it. No questions yet: let it land.

**Do.** Say it once, wait, then click on. No chat move.
:::

## Where does what you type go? {#where-it-goes}

::: {.lane}
[Consumer AI tool: a general assistant you signed up for yourself]{.node .grow} [→]{.op} [Leaves your control]{.node .red .grow}
:::

::: {.lane .fragment}
[Approved tool: one your institution has vetted and contracted]{.node .teal .grow} [→]{.op} [Within the terms your institution gives you]{.node .out .grow}
:::

::: {.fragment}
[▲ The difference is who chose it.]{.pointer}
:::

::: notes
**1:15.** In both lanes you type something. In the top lane the tool is a consumer AI tool: a general assistant you signed up for yourself, such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini on a personal account, and what you typed leaves your control. In the bottom lane it is an approved tool: one your institution has vetted and contracted, and what may go in is bounded by the terms your institution gives you. The difference is who chose it.

**Do.** Click once for the approved lane, once for the line under it. No chat move.
:::

## What the law says, in three sentences {#the-law}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
[Who enforces it]{.t}

SDAIA enforces the PDPL, Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law.
:::
::: {.card .teal}
[What it says about health data]{.t}

Sensitive personal data, alongside genetic and biometric data.
:::
::: {.card .red}
[What it carries]{.t}

Real financial and operational penalties for healthcare entities that mishandle it.
:::
:::

[▲ Education, not legal advice. Ask your institution's data protection officer or legal team.]{.pointer}

::: notes
**0:45.** The law, in three sentences, and stop: Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law, the PDPL, is enforced by SDAIA; it classifies health data as sensitive personal data, like genetic and biometric data; and healthcare entities face real financial and operational penalties for mishandling it. No article numbers, no amounts, no conclusions. I am teaching, not advising: for what applies to you, ask your institution's data protection officer or legal team.

**Do.** Read the three cards, then the line under them. If a legal question comes, park it: that is for the data protection officer or legal team.
:::

## A floor, not a ceiling {#identifier-floor}

If any of these is in what you paste, it is not de-identified.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[]{.chk} Name

[]{.chk} ID or iqama number

[]{.chk} File number

[]{.chk} Phone or email
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
[]{.chk} Address

[]{.chk} Exact date of birth

[]{.chk} Exact dates

[]{.chk} Photograph
:::
:::

[▲ One tick is enough. And the list is only a floor.]{.pointer}

::: notes
**1:15.** This list is a floor, not a ceiling: name, any ID or iqama number, the file number, phone or email, address, exact date of birth, and a photograph. Exact dates count, not only birth dates. Read down both columns and tick them aloud: if any one is in what you paste, it is not de-identified. Then ask what the list cannot catch.

**Do.** Read the boxes down the left, then down the right. No chat move.
:::

## What the list misses {#identifier-combo}

::: {.lane}
[A rare condition]{.node .same .grow} [+]{.op} [A small town]{.node .same .grow} [+]{.op} [A date]{.node .same .grow} [=]{.op} [One person]{.node .red .fixed}
:::

[▲ Any combination of details rare enough to point to one person.]{.pointer}

::: {.card .teal .fragment}
[The test]{.t}

Can a person be identified, directly or indirectly, from what you paste?
:::

::: notes
**1:15.** The one people underestimate is the combination. A rare condition, a small town and a date can each look harmless; together they can point to one person. So the real test is whether a person can be identified, directly or indirectly, from what you paste, by a colleague, a neighbor, or the family. Judge it as a stranger would, and as the family would.

**Do.** Click once for the test. Take a question or two aloud (Speak); keep the chat for the next slides.
:::

## De-identify, then re-read {#deidentify}

::: {.flow}
::: {.step}
[1]{.num} Remove

[every identifier]{.small .muted}
:::
::: {.step}
[2]{.num} Replace

[with neutral labels: "the patient"]{.small .muted}
:::
::: {.step}
[3]{.num} Generalize

[a decade, "outside the city", "day 3"]{.small .muted}
:::
::: {.step}
[4]{.num} Re-read as a stranger

[Could you tell who it is?]{.small .muted}
:::
:::

[▲ Four steps, in this order. The result is a judgment, not a guarantee.]{.pointer}

::: notes
**0:30.** Four steps. Remove every identifier. Replace with neutral labels, such as "the patient". Generalize: an age becomes a decade, a place "outside the city", a date "day 3". Then re-read as a stranger: could you tell who this is? Could someone who knows the family? Next, the routine on a fictional note.

**Do.** Point along the four boxes, left to right. No chat move.
:::

## Mark what points to a person {#deidentify-before}

::: {.card .dashed}
[Before (fictional)]{.t}

[Patient name], 64, file [file number], admitted to [hospital name] on [exact date] with pneumonia and discharged on [exact date]. Lives in [small town]; [her daughter is a nurse on the same ward]{.fragment .highlight-red}.
:::

[▲ The brackets stand for real values that never appear in this course.]{.pointer}

::: {.move .chat}
[Chat · 90 sec]{.tag} Type every identifier, and every detail that could point to one person.
:::

::: notes
**2:00.** Read the note aloud. It is fictional, built on Case B, and the brackets stand for real values that never appear in this course. Chat for 90 seconds: type every identifier, and every detail that could point to one person. Then read out two or three answers.

**Do.** Chat 1:30, answers read out 0:30. Then click once to land on the detail people leave in: the daughter on the ward. Instead of pasting a note like this: an approved tool, de-identify, or a synthetic case.
:::

## After: no one in particular {#deidentify-after}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .red}
[The detail people leave in]{.t}

Her daughter, a nurse on the same ward. It names no one, yet points to someone.
:::
::: {.card .teal .fragment}
[After]{.t}

A woman in her 60s was admitted with pneumonia and discharged on day 4. She lives outside the city with family.
:::
:::

[▲ A judgment, not a guarantee. When in doubt, use a case card.]{.pointer}

::: notes
**0:30.** The last detail in the "before" is the one people leave in. A daughter who is a nurse on the same ward names no one, yet it points to someone, and it adds nothing to the task, so it goes. Click for the after: a woman in her 60s with pneumonia describes no one in particular. Close on the last line: a judgment, not a guarantee.

**Do.** One click for the after. No chat move.
:::

## Beyond the text: where identifiers hide {#formats-that-leak}

::: {.lane .sm}
[Screenshot of the chart]{.node .same .fixed} [→]{.op} [Name, file number, date of birth in the banner]{.node .red .grow}
:::
::: {.lane .sm}
[Photograph]{.node .same .fixed} [→]{.op} [A face, a wristband, a tattoo, a room, a date stamp]{.node .red .grow}
:::
::: {.lane .sm}
[PDF or lab report]{.node .same .fixed} [→]{.op} [Headers, footers, barcodes, the ordering clinician]{.node .red .grow}
:::
::: {.lane .sm}
[Audio recording]{.node .same .fixed} [→]{.op} [A name spoken aloud, a voice]{.node .red .grow}
:::
::: {.lane .sm}
[The filename]{.node .same .fixed} [→]{.op} [The name, carried with the file]{.node .red .grow}
:::

[▲ For example: `FirstName_LastName_discharge_final.docx`]{.pointer}

::: {.move .chat}
[Chat · 45 sec]{.tag} Which of these surprised you? Type one.
:::

::: notes
**1:00.** Identifiers hide outside the text. Walk the five rows in fifteen seconds: the screenshot carries its banner; the photograph a face, a wristband, a tattoo or a date stamp; the lab PDF its headers, footers and barcodes; the recording a spoken name and the voice itself; even the filename can identify. Then the chat.

**Do.** Chat 45 seconds: which of these surprised you? Read out two answers. Do not ask who has done it.
:::

## A setting is not an approval {#settings-dont-approve}

::: {.lane}
[Chat history off, or any privacy setting]{.node .change .grow} [→]{.op} [Still a consumer AI tool]{.node .red .grow}
:::

::: {.lane}
[Your institution vets and contracts it]{.node .teal .grow} [→]{.op} [An approved tool]{.node .out .grow}
:::

[▲ Approval is a decision your institution makes, not a switch you flip.]{.pointer}

::: {.fragment}
[Not sure? Do not paste.]{.big}
:::

::: notes
**0:30.** Turning off chat history, or changing any privacy setting, does not turn a consumer tool into an approved one. Only your institution's approval does: it is a decision your institution makes, not a switch you flip. Close with the habit: not sure, do not paste.

**Do.** Click once for the close. No chat move.
:::

# Where doctors get this wrong [15 min]{.time} {#where-doctors-go-wrong}

::: notes
**Goal.** Everyone can spot the identifier and the path it took in a realistic situation, and name what to do instead.

**Have ready.** A visible timer, and the chat in view.

**Clock.** 0:00 the frame. 0:40, 3:40, 6:40 the three situations. 9:40 the bonus. 11:40 the close. 14:30 time.

**Watch for.** "I would have done the same": treat the motive as reasonable; the fix is a route, not a scolding. The first situation swallowing time: hold three minutes each. A legal debate: park it with the data protection officer or legal team. A real case from someone's own practice, typed or spoken: stop them before any detail and say "keep it general; no real patient goes into this call."

**If asked.** What if the patient consented? Consent to care is not consent to send information to a tool your institution has not approved; whether it changes anything is for your data protection officer or legal team. Everyone in my department does this? Common is not approved; if it has happened, the checklist steps apply, including reporting through your institution's process. A photo of a rash or a scan, no face? Images can carry a face, a tattoo, a wristband, a date stamp or a header; imaging AI is outside this course, so ask what your institution approves.

**Bridge.** "Break, ten minutes. When you come back, have one output from your weekend ready, from Day One or Day Two, not the one from Lab Three. We run the three questions on it."
:::

## Four situations, all invented {#vignette-frame}

::: {.lane .sm}
[Busy]{.node .same} [+]{.op} [The tool was open]{.node .same} [+]{.op} [The shortcut looked harmless]{.node .same} [→]{.op} [A paste]{.node .red}
:::

[▲ Nobody in them is careless.]{.pointer}

::: {.flow}
::: {.step}
[1]{.num} Read the situation
:::
::: {.step}
[2]{.num} Type what is wrong, and what should happen instead
:::
::: {.step}
[3]{.num} Compare with the reveal
:::
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Keep it general
No real patient goes into the chat. Describe a kind of situation, not a person.
:::

::: notes
**0:40.** Four situations, all invented: no real patient, colleague, hospital or incident. The people in them are busy, not careless: the tool was open and the shortcut looked harmless. The routine is the same each time: I read the situation, you type what is wrong and what should happen instead, I read out two answers, then we compare with the reveal. One request: keep it general. No real patient goes into the chat, not even with the name left off. The fourth situation is a bonus; I may skip it if we are short on time.

**Do.** Say it once, then click on. For each situation, invite a volunteer to unmute and read it aloud (Speak), or read it yourself.
:::

## "Just to clean up the wording" {#vignette-cleanup}

[Fictional, invented for this course]{.pill}

::: {.card}
[A physician finishing a long clinic pastes a full discharge summary into a free chatbot on a personal account: "tidy the language before I sign."]{.big}
:::

::: {.move .chat}
[Chat · 90 sec]{.tag} Type what is wrong, and what should happen instead.
:::

::: notes
**2:00.** Read the situation aloud, or ask a volunteer to unmute and read it (Speak). Then run the chat for 90 seconds: type what is wrong, and what should happen instead. Push for the specifics as answers come in: which identifiers, and where did they go? Leave the reveal until most have typed.

**Do.** Chat 1:30. Do not ask who has done this.
:::

## The paste was the slip {#vignette-cleanup-path}

::: {.lane}
[A long clinic, a full summary to sign]{.node .same .grow} [→]{.op} [Pasted into a free chatbot, personal account]{.node .red .grow} [→]{.op} ["Tidy the language before I sign"]{.node .same .grow}
:::

[▲ A full clinical picture, with identifiers, went to a tool nobody vetted. Deleting the chat does not undo it.]{.pointer}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .teal .fragment}
[What should happen instead]{.t}

Use the approved tool, or write it yourself. Paste only de-identified text or a synthetic case.
:::
::: {.card .dark .fragment}
**The line.** Take the wording to the tool. Leave the patient behind.
:::
:::

::: notes
**1:00.** Read out two answers, then show the path. The summary opens with the name and file number, then the dates, the family's town, the diagnoses and the medicines: identifiers attached to a full clinical picture. It went from the institution's records to a personal account on a consumer tool nobody vetted or contracted, and deleting the chat does not undo it. The tidied text also comes back unchecked, so Module 6 applies: check it against the original before signing. Then the line.

**Do.** Answers 0:30, then two clicks: what to do instead, the line.
:::

[Fictional, invented for this course]{.pill}

## The banner was in the picture {#vignette-screenshot-banner}

::: {.card .dashed}
[A screenshot of a lab result]{.t}

::: {.lane .sm}
[Name]{.node .red .grow} [File number]{.node .red .grow} [Date of birth]{.node .red .grow}
:::
::: {.lane .sm}
[Lab result: the values asked about]{.node .same .grow}
:::
::: {.lane .sm}
[A report may add a barcode and the ordering clinician]{.node .ghost .grow}
:::
:::

[▲ The banner carries the name, file number and date of birth.]{.pointer} [Illustrative: drawn for this course, not a real record]{.illustrative}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .teal .fragment}
[What should happen instead]{.t}

Ask a senior colleague, or retype only the values you need into an approved tool, with no dates.
:::
::: {.card .dark .fragment}
**The line.** The banner is part of the picture.
:::
:::

::: notes
**1:00.** Read out two answers, then show the mock. The banner carries the name, file number and date of birth, and the report may add a barcode and the ordering clinician. Nothing identifying was typed and it left anyway, because an image carries everything inside it. Cropping helps only if you have checked every other part of the image and the file's metadata. The answer that comes back is a draft: the doctor decides. Instead: ask a senior colleague through the institution's own channels, or retype only the values you need, age as a decade and no dates, into an approved tool if there is one, and check any answer against a primary source.

**Do.** Answers 0:30, then two clicks.
:::

## Two disclosures, one visit {#vignette-phone-scribe-path}

::: {.lane}
[The visit: a name, a voice, what the family said]{.node .same .grow} [→]{.op} [Free phone app]{.node .red .grow} [→]{.op} [Transcript pasted into a chatbot]{.node .red .grow}
:::

[▲ Two services no institution approved. The patient was never told.]{.pointer}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .teal .fragment}
[What should happen instead]{.t}

Use the scribe your institution approved. If there is none, write the note yourself.
:::
::: {.card .dark .fragment}
**The line.** A scribe is approved by your institution, not by how well it works.
:::
:::

::: notes
**1:00.** Read out two answers, then show the path. The recording holds a name spoken aloud, a voice, and everything the family said. It lands on a free app's servers, then, as a transcript, in a second consumer tool: two disclosures, both to services no institution approved. The Day Two scribes were put in place by institutions; that was the institution's decision, not an individual doctor's, and it is the difference. Instead: use the scribe your institution approved, the way it says. If there is none, take your own notes, write the note yourself, and ask whether one is planned.

**Do.** Answers 0:30, then two clicks.
:::

## No name, and still one family {#vignette-anonymized-path}

::: {.lane .sm}
[No name: step one of four]{.node .same .grow} [+]{.op} [A child with a very rare condition]{.node .red .grow} [+]{.op} [The small town]{.node .red .grow} [+]{.op} [The exact admission date]{.node .red .grow}
:::

[▲ Each may pass alone. Together they point to one family.]{.pointer}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .teal .fragment}
[What should happen instead]{.t}

Generalize: an age band, a region, "day 3". If the rare condition gives it away, change the story.
:::
::: {.card .dark .fragment}
**The line.** No name is not the same as no identity.
:::
:::

::: notes
**0:45.** Read out two answers, then show the path. Each detail might pass alone; together they point to one family. That is what "any combination of details rare enough to point to one person" means. Removing the name was step one of four. Instead: generalize until the details point nowhere, an age band, a region, "day 3" for a date. If the rare condition is the giveaway and the teaching point survives without it, keep the point and change the story: that makes it a synthetic case. Unsure: ask the data protection officer.

**Do.** Answers, then two clicks.
:::

## Before any paste, ask {#before-you-paste}

::: {.lane}
[Is this tool approved for patient information?]{.node .grow} [no →]{.op} [Is it synthetic, or fully de‑identified?]{.node .grow} [no →]{.op} [Do not paste]{.node .red .fixed}
:::

[▲ If you cannot say yes, do not paste.]{.pointer}

[Instead:]{.teal} [an approved tool]{.pill .teal} [de-identify, then re-read]{.pill .teal} [a synthetic case]{.pill .teal}

::: notes
**0:30.** Before any paste, two questions. Is this tool approved for patient information? If not, is what I am pasting synthetic or fully de-identified, with no identifier in the text or the file, and nothing that would let someone who knows this person recognize them? If you cannot say yes, do not paste. Instead: an approved tool, de-identify, or a synthetic case.

**Do.** Point along the lane. No chat move.
:::

## If it already happened {#if-it-happened}

::: {.lane}
[1 Stop]{.node .grow} [→]{.op} [2 Write down what was pasted, into which tool, and when]{.node .grow} [→]{.op} [3 Report it: your institution's process, and its data protection officer]{.node .teal .grow}
:::

[▲ Do not assume deleting the chat undoes it.]{.pointer}

::: notes
**0:20.** If it already happened: stop, write down what was pasted, into which tool and when, and report it through your institution's process and to its data protection officer. Do not assume deleting the chat undoes it. The steps are on the privacy checklist, linked on the last slide.

**Do.** Say it plainly, with no blame. No chat move.
:::
